_umrli_1774_1804._folio_map_MEASURED: READ THE PRINTED FOLIO NUMBER — top outer corner of each page. Measured anchors: folio 17 = image 364 right; folio 38 = image 376 LEFT and folio 39 its right; folio 63 = image 388 right; folio 64 = image 389 left (Anno Domini 1790); folio 74 = image 394 left (Anno Domini 1793). From image 376 to 394 it is EXACTLY two folios per image; between 364 and 376 it is not, so a formula fitted at one end lands a leaf out at the other. Interpolate, then read the number and step.
_umrli_1774_1804._kazalo: The volume's own A-Z index sits at images ~410-434. The big letter is written across the top of the page and lands visually over the SECOND column group, but it governs the whole page. Measured: image 427 right = P, 428 left = P (tail, folios 104-106 only) and right = R, 429 right = S, 430 right = T, 432 right = V. Entries within a letter run BY FOLIO, not alphabetically, so a surname is found by scanning the letter's columns. Letter positions measured so far: G = image 418 right page (419 left is G and EMPTY); P = 427 right and 428 left; R = 428 right; S = 429 right; T = 430 right; V = 432 right. A letter's entries sit in the columns of ONE page and the big letter is written across the top, so an empty-looking page means the letter is on the opening before it.
_umrli_1774_1804._why_the_kazalo: The FamilySearch record index holds baptisms only for Karlobag (row 43), so this book must be walked — but its own index turns a walk into two page loads.

found.ahn 104: «Pillepich Jacobus · 10 Aprilis · folio 17» in the KAZALO (image 427) → folio 17, image 364: «10: Aprilis · D. Jacobus Pilepich Capitaneus portûs, munitus omnibus Sacramentis per M.R. D. Andream Pintor Capellanum Loci, spiritum Deo reddidit … in propria Crypta in Parochiali Ecclesia existente … tumulatus est». No age. See notes/karlobag-1778-jacobus-pilepich.md.
found.ahn 212: «Vukich vide Smojver, 16: Maij, folio 11» in the KAZALO (image 432, letter V) -> folio 11, image 361: «16 ejusdem [Maij 1776] · Josephus Smojver dictus Vukcich, annorum 45, munitus omnibus [Sacramentis] … in Domino obijt, atque die 17 … in Coemeterio Parochiali tumulatus». 16 May 1776 is the tree's date to the day and annorum 45 agrees with its 1731. NOTE: the S columns were read only to about folio 9 — the sitting turned to V before reaching folio 11, so the Smojver headword was never checked.
found.ahn 220: «Gergacs Nicolaus · 3i 8bris · folio 39» in the KAZALO (image 418, letter G) -> folio 39, image 376: «30 8bris · Nicolaus Gergacs annorum 66, munitus omnibus sacramentis obiit … in domo filij sui Antonij, et die 31: ejusdem … sepultus est in Cœmeterio … Laterali ex parte dextra Ecclesiæ Parochialis hujus». 30 October 1783 is the tree's date to the day, and annorum 66 agrees with its 1717. He died IN HIS SON ANTONIUS'S HOUSE — a Gergacs the tree does not publish.
found.ahn 105: NOT in the KAZALO's L section. Found by walking the register instead: folio 63, image 388, «29 ejusdem [Maij 1790] · Catharina annorum 70, vidua defti Jacobi [P]ilepich, obiit in Domino munita omnibus sacramentis, atque die 30 sepulta est». The tree's date to the day, and she is named as the widow of ahnentafel 104 — which is what identifies her. THE AGE DISAGREES: 70 in May 1790 puts her birth about 1720 where the tree says 30 March 1727.

_umrli_1774_1804._kazalo_indexes_bynames: IMPORTANT. The KAZALO indexes HOUSEHOLD BY-NAMES as headwords and cross-references them to the surname with «vide». «Vukich vide Smojver, 16: Maij, folio 11» is how ahnentafel 212 was found; the same page carries «Verbanovich Margarita … vide Urbanovich, 15 9bris». A surname missing from its own letter is NOT absent from the book — look under the household by-name in another letter.
_umrli_1774_1804._kazalo_date_is_the_burial: IMPORTANT. The KAZALO's date can be the BURIAL, not the death. It gives «Gergacs Nicolaus 3i 8bris» where the register says he died on the 30th and was buried «die 31: ejusdem». The archive already knew this shape from Find a Grave — a cemetery records the interment, a parish records the death — and the KAZALO does it too. Use the index date to FIND the entry, never to record one.

_umrli_1774_1804._widows_are_indexed_under_the_husband: The whole L section was read — groups 1 and 2 of image 422's right page, folios 1-73 and 76-102, group 3 blank, and image 423's left page (also headed L) is empty. Five Luckinić entries are there — Lukcrinich Lucas f.2, Luczkinich Anton f.7, Luczkinich Helena f.38, Luczkinich Antonia vidua f.84, Luczkinich Helena f.96 — and NONE is Catharina. She is a widow, and a widow is indexed under HER HUSBAND'S surname: look for her in P. Same shape as «Vukich vide Smojver», and the same shape as the Senj gravestones, where a married woman is carved under her husband's name.
